We grilled chicken on the ____ in the garden.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'Laid-back'?

words.english_meaning: Salty or spicy in taste, rather than sweet.
words.gujarati_meaning: મીઠું/તીખું (ગળ્યું નહિ) સ્વાદવાળું.
words.usage_note: Opposite of 'sweet'; e.g. samosas are savoury. (US spelling: 'savory'.)
examples: I prefer savoury snacks to sweets.
She made a savoury pie for dinner.
The menu has both sweet and savoury options.
These crackers have a nice savoury flavour.

words.english_meaning: Having little or no strong flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: સ્વાદ વગરનું, ફિક્કું.
words.usage_note: Negative for taste; food that needs more seasoning.
examples: The soup was bland and needed salt.
Hospital food can be quite bland.
He found the curry too bland.
Add some spices so it isn't bland.

words.english_meaning: Having a strong, sharp, pleasant taste, often sour or citrusy.
words.gujarati_meaning: તીખાશભર્યો, ખટમધુરો સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: Pleasantly sharp — like lemon, tamarind, or yoghurt.
examples: The tangy lemon dressing was delicious.
I love the tangy taste of tamarind.
The sauce had a nice tangy kick.
Yoghurt gives the dish a tangy flavour.

words.english_meaning: Looking or smelling so delicious that it makes you want to eat it.
words.gujarati_meaning: મોઢામાં પાણી લાવી દે એવું સ્વાદિષ્ટ.
words.usage_note: Strong positive for how food looks or smells.
examples: The mouth-watering smell of biryani filled the house.
The menu had a mouth-watering selection.
She showed me a mouth-watering photo of the cake.
Those sweets look absolutely mouth-watering.

words.english_meaning: (Of food) containing a lot of fat, cream, sugar, or spices; heavy.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘી/ક્રીમ/ખાંડથી ભરપૂર, ભારે.
words.usage_note: Here 'rich' means heavy/indulgent food, not money.
examples: The chocolate cake was very rich.
This gravy is rich and creamy.
A rich meal can feel heavy.
The dessert was too rich for me.

words.english_meaning: No longer fresh, especially of bread or other food.
words.gujarati_meaning: વાસી, તાજું ન રહેલું.
words.usage_note: 'Go stale' = become old/dry. Opposite of 'fresh'.
examples: The bread had gone stale.
Don't eat those stale biscuits.
Stale food can upset your stomach.
The cake tasted stale after a week.

words.english_meaning: Having a fresh, lively, often citrus-like flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: તાજગીભર્યો, લીંબુ જેવો ચટપટો સ્વાદ.
words.usage_note: Suggests bright, refreshing flavour (often lemon/lime). 'Zest' = citrus peel.
examples: The salad had a zesty lime dressing.
I added orange zest for a zesty taste.
It's a light, zesty summer drink.
The marinade gives the fish a zesty flavour.

words.english_meaning: To cook gently in liquid just below boiling point.
words.gujarati_meaning: ધીમા તાપે ઉકાળવું (ઉકળતા પહેલાંના તાપે).
words.usage_note: Slow, gentle cooking with small bubbles, not a rolling boil.
examples: Let the curry simmer for twenty minutes.
Simmer the sauce gently until it thickens.
The soup simmered on the stove.
Reduce the heat and let it simmer.

words.english_meaning: To fry food quickly in a small amount of hot fat or oil.
words.gujarati_meaning: થોડા તેલમાં ઝડપથી તળવું / સાંતળવું.
words.usage_note: Quick frying over high heat. (French; said 'SOH-tay'.)
examples: Sauté the onions until golden.
She sautéed the vegetables in butter.
Lightly sauté the garlic first.
The mushrooms were sautéed to perfection.

words.english_meaning: To soak food in a seasoned liquid before cooking to add flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: મસાલાવાળા પ્રવાહીમાં પલાળી રાખવું.
words.usage_note: The liquid itself is the 'marinade'. Adds flavour and tenderness.
examples: Marinate the chicken overnight for best flavour.
We marinated the paneer in spices.
The meat needs to marinate for an hour.
She marinated the fish in lemon and herbs.

words.english_meaning: To beat eggs, cream, or a mixture quickly to add air.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઝડપથી ફીણવું / ફેંટવું (ઈંડા/ક્રીમ).
words.usage_note: Both a verb and the wire tool used for it.
examples: Whisk the eggs until fluffy.
Whisk the batter to remove lumps.
She whisked the cream into soft peaks.
Whisk together the flour and milk.

words.english_meaning: To press and stretch dough with your hands until smooth.
words.gujarati_meaning: લોટ/કણક હાથથી મસળવું.
words.usage_note: The 'k' is silent — said 'need'. Essential for bread/roti dough.
examples: Knead the dough for ten minutes.
She kneaded the flour into a soft dough.
Keep kneading until it's smooth.
Well-kneaded dough makes soft rotis.

words.english_meaning: To add salt, pepper, or spices to food to improve its flavour.
words.gujarati_meaning: મીઠું-મસાલા ઉમેરવા.
words.usage_note: 'Season to taste' = add as much as you like. Noun 'seasoning' = the spices.
examples: Season the soup with salt and pepper.
Don't forget to season the rice.
Season to taste before serving.
She seasoned the curry generously.

words.english_meaning: To decorate food with a small amount of something to make it look attractive.
words.gujarati_meaning: સજાવટ માટે ઉપર પાથરવું / શણગારવું.
words.usage_note: Both a verb and a noun (the decoration itself).
examples: Garnish the dish with fresh coriander.
She garnished the soup with cream.
A garnish of lemon adds colour.
The chef garnished the plate with herbs.

words.english_meaning: A style or method of cooking, especially of a particular country or region.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ પ્રદેશ/સંસ્કૃતિની રસોઈ-શૈલી.
words.usage_note: Refers to a cooking tradition. (French; said 'kwi-ZEEN'.)
examples: I love Italian cuisine.
The restaurant serves South Indian cuisine.
We tried the local cuisine on holiday.
Thai cuisine is known for its bold flavours.

words.english_meaning: A small dish served before the main course to start a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: મુખ્ય ભોજન પહેલાંની હળવી વાનગી / સ્ટાર્ટર.
words.usage_note: The starter course. (US spelling: 'appetizer'.)
examples: We shared an appetiser before the meal.
The soup was served as an appetiser.
Try the spring rolls as an appetiser.
Appetisers are listed at the top of the menu.

words.english_meaning: The largest or most important dish of a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભોજનની મુખ્ય વાનગી.
words.usage_note: Comes after the appetiser and before dessert.
examples: For the main course, I had grilled fish.
The main course was served with rice.
We skipped the main course and went to dessert.
What will you have as a main course?

words.english_meaning: A drink, especially one other than water.
words.usage_note: A formal word for a drink; common on menus.
examples: Would you like a hot beverage?
The menu lists several cold beverages.
Tea is my favourite beverage.
Alcoholic beverages are not served here.

words.english_meaning: A note showing how much you must pay for a meal at a restaurant.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભોજનનું બિલ / હિસાબ.
words.usage_note: UK 'the bill', US 'the check'. 'Split the bill' = share the cost.
examples: Could we have the bill, please?
He kindly paid the bill.
Let's split the bill evenly.
The waiter brought the bill to our table.

words.english_meaning: A small extra amount of money given to someone for good service.
words.gujarati_meaning: સેવા બદલ અપાતી બક્ષિસ.
words.usage_note: Both noun and verb ('tip the waiter'). Extra money for good service.
examples: We left a generous tip for the waiter.
It's polite to tip for good service.
The service was poor, so we left no tip.
She tipped the driver a little extra.

words.english_meaning: An arrangement to have a table, room, or seat kept for you.
words.gujarati_meaning: ટેબલ/જગ્યા અગાઉથી બુક કરાવવી.
words.usage_note: 'Make/have a reservation' for a table or room.
examples: I made a reservation for two at eight.
Do you have a reservation, sir?
We had to cancel our dinner reservation.
It's wise to book a reservation on weekends.

words.english_meaning: Containing many of the substances the body needs to stay healthy.
words.gujarati_meaning: પોષણયુક્ત, શરીરને ફાયદાકારક.
words.usage_note: Food that is good for you. Noun: 'nutrition'.
examples: Vegetables are very nutritious.
She cooks nutritious meals for the family.
A nutritious breakfast keeps you energetic.
Fruits are a nutritious snack.

words.english_meaning: Good for your health; healthy and nourishing.
words.gujarati_meaning: તંદુરસ્ત, શરીર માટે સારું.
words.usage_note: Suggests simple, natural, healthy food.
examples: They serve wholesome, home-style food.
Oats make a wholesome breakfast.
We prefer wholesome ingredients.
A wholesome diet keeps you fit.

words.english_meaning: An amount of food served to or eaten by one person.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વ્યક્તિ માટેનો ભોજનનો ભાગ / હિસ્સો.
words.usage_note: 'Portion size' = how much is served. Controlling portions helps health.
examples: The restaurant serves large portions.
Watch your portion sizes.
She gave me a small portion of rice.
Divide the cake into equal portions.

words.english_meaning: To have a very strong desire for a particular food.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ ખાવાની તીવ્ર ઇચ્છા થવી.
words.usage_note: 'Crave' + food; noun 'craving' = a strong urge.
examples: I'm craving something sweet.
She craves spicy food when stressed.
Pregnant women often crave odd foods.
After the gym, I crave a big meal.

words.english_meaning: To eat more food than you need or than is healthy.
words.gujarati_meaning: જરૂર કરતાં વધારે ખાવું.
words.usage_note: Eating too much; common at feasts/festivals.
examples: It's easy to overeat at a buffet.
I always overeat during festivals.
Try not to overeat before bed.
He overate and felt uncomfortable.

words.english_meaning: A way of eating that includes the right variety and amount of foods for health.
words.gujarati_meaning: પોષક તત્ત્વોથી ભરપૂર સંતુલિત આહાર.
words.usage_note: Includes carbs, protein, fats, and vitamins in proper proportion.
examples: A balanced diet keeps you healthy.
Doctors recommend a balanced diet.
She follows a balanced diet and exercises.
Children need a balanced diet to grow.

words.english_meaning: Extremely hungry.
words.gujarati_meaning: અતિશય ભૂખ્યું.
words.usage_note: A strong word for very hungry (stronger than 'hungry').
examples: I'm famished — let's eat now.
After the hike, we were all famished.
He looked famished and tired.
By lunchtime she was absolutely famished.

words.english_meaning: Slightly hungry.
words.usage_note: Informal British; mildly hungry — wanting a snack.
examples: I'm feeling a bit peckish.
If you're peckish, have some fruit.
We were peckish, so we shared a snack.
A peckish child kept asking for biscuits.

words.english_meaning: The natural desire to eat food.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભૂખ, ખાવાની ઇચ્છા.
words.usage_note: 'Lose your appetite' = not feel like eating.
examples: The walk gave me a good appetite.
He has a healthy appetite.
I lost my appetite when I felt ill.
The aroma whetted our appetite.

words.english_meaning: Having eaten enough; not able to eat any more.
words.gujarati_meaning: પેટ ભરાઈ ગયું હોવું.
words.usage_note: Informal for 'I've eaten enough'.
examples: No more for me, I'm full up.
We were full up after the feast.
I can't finish this — I'm full up.
The kids said they were full up.

words.english_meaning: To eat something by taking small bites.
words.gujarati_meaning: થોડું થોડું, ધીમે ધીમે ખાવું.
words.usage_note: Eating slowly in tiny bites; 'nibble on' a snack.
examples: She nibbled on a biscuit.
We nibbled at the snacks while chatting.
The mouse nibbled the cheese.
He nibbled his food without much appetite.

words.english_meaning: To eat something quickly and hungrily.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભૂખ્યાની જેમ ઝડપથી ખાઈ જવું.
words.usage_note: Eating fast and eagerly; the opposite of 'nibble'.
examples: The children devoured the pizza.
He devoured his dinner in minutes.
We were so hungry we devoured everything.
She devoured the cake hungrily.

words.english_meaning: A rare or special food that is considered especially nice to eat.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ ખાસ/દુર્લભ સ્વાદિષ્ટ વાનગી.
words.usage_note: A prized, often regional special food.
examples: This sweet is a local delicacy.
Fish curry is a delicacy in this region.
We tasted several delicacies on the trip.
Caviar is considered a delicacy.

words.english_meaning: A portion of food given to one person at a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વાર પીરસાતો ભોજનનો ભાગ.
words.usage_note: 'A second helping' = more of the same dish.
examples: Can I have a second helping, please?
She gave me a generous helping of rice.
He took a large helping of dessert.
There's enough for second helpings.

words.english_meaning: Made at home, not bought from a shop.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘરે બનાવેલું.
words.usage_note: Implies fresh, personal cooking. (Also written 'home-made'.)
examples: I love homemade pickles.
The cake was homemade.
Homemade food is healthier.
She brought homemade cookies to share.

words.english_meaning: (Of food or drink) very hot.
words.gujarati_meaning: એકદમ ગરમાગરમ.
words.usage_note: An idiom for freshly cooked, very hot food.
examples: The soup was served piping hot.
Enjoy the rotis piping hot.
She brought out a piping hot pizza.
Nothing beats piping hot tea on a cold day.

words.english_meaning: To eat something quickly, often a small or casual meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઝડપથી થોડું ખાઈ લેવું.
words.usage_note: Informal — a quick, casual meal.
words.memory_tip: ઝડપથી થોડું ખાઈ લેવું = grab a bite.
examples: Let's grab a bite before the movie.
I only had time to grab a bite.
We grabbed a bite at a roadside stall.
Want to grab a bite after work?

words.english_meaning: To have a meal at a restaurant rather than at home.
words.gujarati_meaning: બહાર (રેસ્ટોરન્ટમાં) જમવું.
words.usage_note: The opposite of 'eat in' / 'cook at home'.
examples: Let's eat out tonight.
We eat out once a week.
They prefer eating out on weekends.
It's cheaper to cook than to eat out.

words.english_meaning: To start eating something eagerly and with enjoyment.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભૂખથી/ઉત્સાહથી ખાવાનું શરૂ કરવું.
words.usage_note: Informal British; 'tuck into' a meal = eat it heartily.
examples: The food's ready — tuck in!
They tucked into the feast happily.
He tucked into a big plate of biryani.
Don't wait for me; tuck in.

mini_dialogues.title: Deciding to eat out
mini_dialogues.situation: Two friends plan dinner.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm famished. Shall we eat out tonight?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Sure! I've been craving some good Italian cuisine.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Let me make a reservation for two.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Great — I could really tuck into a big bowl of pasta.

mini_dialogues.title: At the restaurant
mini_dialogues.situation: Ordering a meal with a waiter.

turns.speaker: Waiter
turns.text: What will you have as a main course?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The grilled fish, please, and a cold beverage.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Shall we order an appetiser to share?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes — and let's remember to leave a tip.

mini_dialogues.title: Cooking at home
mini_dialogues.situation: You praise a friend's home cooking.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: This homemade curry smells mouth-watering!

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Thanks. I let it simmer and seasoned it well.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Did you garnish it with coriander?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Of course. Tuck in while it's piping hot!

mini_dialogues.title: Eating healthily
mini_dialogues.situation: Talking about diet.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm trying to follow a balanced diet.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Good idea — eat more nutritious, wholesome food.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: But I still crave sweets sometimes.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: A small portion now and then is fine.

mini_dialogues.title: A snack break
mini_dialogues.situation: Offering a snack before dinner.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Are you hungry?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Just a little peckish, actually.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There are some biscuits — nibble on those for now.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Thanks. I don't want to overeat before dinner.
